newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Jail sex traffickers longer, EU says.
newsitem.headline: Jail sex traffickers longer, EU says.

text.p: Criminals who traffic in women for sex should get stiffer prison sentences, the European Commission said on Wednesday.

Accusing EU governments of brushing the problem under the carpet, European Justice Commissioner Anita Gradin said that while a convicted drug trafficker could expect 10 years in jail, someone found selling women might get only two.

Hundreds of thousands of women, mainly from central and eastern Europe but also from Asia and Latin America, were being lured to the European Union with the promise of better lives, the Swedish commissioner said.
Once there they were forced into a situation of dependency and made to work as prostitutes. Light sentences and the difficulty of convicting pimps and traffickers made he trade attractive.
"Trafficking in women is a growing and very profitable business for those in organised crime," she told a news conference to unveil a Commission action.

The Commission wants EU countries to grant temporary residence permits -- as is currently the case in Belgium and the Netherlands -- to allow women forced into prostitution to testify against their captors.
"A temporary permit of stay is necessary to help the victims to recuperate and to testify against the traffickers," the Commission said in a statement.
Such cases are hard to prosecute because women who have entered the country illegally are often unwilling to testify.
Gradin said that captive women were often mistreated and in danger of contracting AIDS.
The Commission also intends to finance campaigns in eastern Europe to spread the word about the risks of job offers for waitresses, dancers, hostesses and au pairs in the EU.

It also called for training programmes for immigration and asylum officers, social and health workers and police officers and the setting up of reception and rehabilitation centres in both EU and eastern European countries.
